entries.title: Amos 2:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The bones - Or ashes, reduced them by fire into fine dust, and used these ashes instead of lime to plaister the walls and roofs of his palace, and this in hatred and contempt of the king of Edom.

entries.title: Amos 2:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Kirioth - A principal city of this country. Moab - The Moabites. Shall die - Be destroyed. With tumult - Such as soldiers in fight or assaults make, when they carry all by force.

entries.title: Amos 2:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The judge - The governor that is, every one of them.

entries.title: Amos 2:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Lies - Idols. To err - Their idolatry blinded them, partly from the natural tendency of this sin, and partly from the just judgment of God. After which - Idols. Walked - Successively, one generation after another.

entries.title: Amos 2:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Shoes - The smallest bribe, exprest here proverbially.

entries.title: Amos 2:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The people - That make a prey even of the poor afflicted ones, who walk with dust on their heads. Turn aside - Maliciously interpret the actions, words, and designs of the humble and meek. Will go in - These corrupt judges commit also that lewdness which the Heathens abhor.

entries.title: Amos 2:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Lay down - The Jews of old did not sit upright at their meals, but leaned on one side. Upon clothes - Of which the law had expressly said, none should detain them all night, Deut 24:12,13. Every altar - Of their idols. Drink the wine - They offer their drink - offerings in wine, which they bought with the fines laid on the innocent.

entries.title: Amos 2:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The Ammorite - The mightiest nation of all the Canaanites. As the oaks - Another proverbial speech denoting their great strength. His fruit - Their children. His roots - The old standards; that present generation.

entries.title: Amos 2:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Nazarites - Persons who bound themselves to a very sober and holy life; either for some certain time, or for their whole life.

entries.title: Amos 2:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Ye gave - Importuned them to drink wine, to violate their vow, and contemn God's law.

entries.title: Amos 2:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Under you - Under the load of your sins.

entries.title: Amos 2:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The swift - For their enemies shall be swifter than they. The strong - Natural strength of body shall not deliver. The mighty - The valiant man, the man of the greatest courage.
